steps.title: Configure LI‑6800 with aquatic chamber
steps.instruction: Install the LI‑6800 portable photosynthesis system with aquatic chamber 6800‑18, attach the sample adaptor kit (LI‑COR part no. 9968‑338) that holds 1 mL of media, orient the sensor head handle up so duckweed lies parallel to airflow, connect a recirculating water bath to the chamber ports for temperature control, and set instrument constants: flow 500 µmol s⁻¹ (pump auto), humidity 70 %, reference CO₂ (C_a) 400 µmol mol⁻¹, T_exchange 25 °C, mixing fan speed 10 000 rpm.

steps.title: Perform instrument warm‑up tests
steps.instruction: Replenish instrument chemicals (soda lime, sorbeads, water), attach a new CO₂ canister, verify that chamber plugs are replaced, ensure the aquatic pump is OFF and the adaptor well contains no media, then run the LI‑COR warm‑up tests and resolve any issues according to the manufacturer’s guidance.

steps.title: Hydrate membrane and stabilize IRGAs
steps.instruction: Turn the aquatic pump ON (keep ON while media are present), load the adaptor well with 1 mL of N‑Medium (or water), confirm the environmental constants set in step 1, and let the LI‑6800 operate for approximately 1 hour to allow the IRGAs to warm up and reach stability.

steps.title: Load duckweed into adaptor well
steps.instruction: Remove the 1 mL of media from the adaptor well and replace it with fresh media, transfer duckweed fronds into the well using an inoculating loop so they cover most of the surface, and wait 2–15 minutes for gas exchange to reach steady state (≈2 min if chamber conditions match growth conditions, up to 15 min if CO₂ or light are much higher).

steps.title: Set light intensity accounting for loss
steps.instruction: Recognize that incident light on the sample (Q_sample) is about 50 % of the programmed Q_in due to internal losses; the maximum Q_sample achievable is ≈1611 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹. Calculate required Q_in for desired Q_sample using Equations 1‑3 and Table 1, and set Q_in values according to Table 2 for subsequent light curves.

steps.title: Measure subsample flow and apply CO₂ correction
steps.instruction: Measure the subsample flow rate following the LI‑COR 6800‑18 user manual (page 100). Compute the actual ΔCO₂ using Equation 4 and then calculate the headspace atmospheric CO₂ mole fraction (C_a) with Equation 5, employing the component definitions in Table 3.

steps.title: Run light‑response curve
steps.instruction: Equilibrate duckweed at high light 2979.52 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ for 10‑15 minutes until steady state, run AUTO MATCH from the Measurement tab, then execute a light‑response program with Q_sample setpoints 1600, 1400, 1200, 1000, 800, 600, 400, 200, 100, 50, 0 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ (Q_in values per Table 2). Set minimum and maximum wait times to 120 s and 180 s respectively; total runtime ≤39 minutes. Optionally average the signal over 20‑45 seconds in the Log setup.

steps.title: Run CO₂‑response curve
steps.instruction: Set saturating light to 1000 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ at the sample (Q_in = 1862.20 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹). After 10‑15 minutes equilibration, run AUTO MATCH, then run a CO₂‑response program with reference C_a setpoints 400, 300, 200, 100, 50, 0, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1400 µmol mol⁻¹. Use minimum/maximum wait times of 600 s and 660 s; total runtime ≤2 h 34 min. Matching is required at each CO₂ level.

steps.title: Conduct temperature‑response series
steps.instruction: Configure light to 1000 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ at the sample (Q_in = 1862.20 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹), CO₂ 400 µmol mol⁻¹, RH 70 %. Attach a recirculating water bath and start at the lowest temperature 17.5 °C (T_exchange set equal). After adding duckweed, allow CO₂ flux to reach steady state (10‑15 minutes), run AUTO MATCH, then log the average CO₂ flux over the previous 45 seconds. Increase water‑bath temperature sequentially to 20, 22.5, 25, 27.5, 30, 32.5, 35, 37.5 °C; each step requires ~15 minutes for the bath to reach setpoint, then hold T_aquatic for 300 seconds before logging. AUTO MATCH is run a few minutes before each log. Total runtime ≈3 hours.

steps.title: Perform instantaneous survey measurements
steps.instruction: Set environmental conditions to Q_sample = 1000 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ (Q_in = 1862.2 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹), temperature 25 °C, RH 70 %, CO₂ 400 µmol mol⁻¹. Record data every 5 minutes from 07:00 to 23:00. Replace the CO₂ canister and N‑Medium in the adaptor well at the midpoint of the measurement period.

steps.title: Normalize data by area and biomass
steps.instruction: Normalize gas‑exchange results: (a) Image duckweed from above with a ruler, set scale in ImageJ, and calculate 2‑D surface area using colour‑threshold tools; (b) Measure fresh weight with a milligram‑precision balance; (c) Flash‑freeze samples in liquid nitrogen and freeze‑dry for 16 hours to obtain dry weight; (d) Determine chlorophyll a + b from freeze‑dried material following Lichtenthaler & Babani (2022).
